title: Microsoft Restores Outlook, Teams and Copilot After Outage Lasting Over 36 Hours
excerpt: Microsoft confirmed early Saturday that corrective work is complete after a network fault disrupted Microsoft 365 in more than 70 countries, though delayed email is still being cleared and a full post-incident report is pending.
body:
• Microsoft confirmed early on Saturday, November 14, that it had completed corrective work and restored Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services after a global outage lasting more than 36 hours.
  • The company traced the fault to an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced after a recent network change, and said it was not a cyberattack and not caused by AI agents.
  • The disruption began on Thursday, November 12, with Exchange Online mailbox failures and spread to SharePoint, Planner and To Do, affecting users in more than 70 countries.
  • For readers still missing mail: Microsoft restored services in stages and extended the email timeout window to 48 hours while it clears delayed traffic, so check the Microsoft service health status page before assuming a message is lost.

Microsoft has restored its services after a global outage that lasted more than 36 hours, the company confirmed early on Saturday, November 14. Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 applications are operational again, according to the company, ending a disruption that began on Thursday, November 12, and affected users in more than 70 countries. Microsoft said customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer experience disruption, although it is continuing to monitor its systems and clear delayed email traffic.

What is new: restoration, in stages

The restoration is the development that closes the episode this site reported on Friday, when the outage rolled into a second day. Microsoft said it brought services back in stages, checking system stability at each step rather than attempting a simultaneous restart. It also extended the email timeout window to 48 hours to accommodate delayed messages while backlogs were being processed. The company apologised to affected customers and partners and promised a detailed post-incident report once its review is complete.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ogzNYEXjWlA

On its service health status page, Microsoft listed consumer products as operational in the latest update available during this reporting. The company said it was seeing broad recovery and stability across its services, while continuing to restore service to any remaining customers and regions and to monitor email queues.

What caused the outage

Microsoft traced the problem to a technical fault linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade. The issue emerged after a subsequent network change, according to the company. It ruled out a cyberattack and said artificial intelligence agents were not responsible.

"This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change."

— Microsoft, in an update quoted by Power Corridors

The fault started with Exchange Online, Microsoft's cloud email platform. Users first reported problems accessing their mailboxes on Thursday, and the disruption then spread to services that depend on Exchange Online. Teams continued to support basic messaging and online meetings, but functions linked to Exchange Online, including calendars and meeting scheduling, were disrupted. Copilot users reported difficulties loading conversations and retrieving workplace information stored in emails, calendars and files. SharePoint, Planner and To Do were also affected.

How India was affected

In India, IndiGo said its email support system had been affected and warned that it might not receive customer messages. The airline advised passengers seeking urgent assistance to use its website or mobile application. Air India, by contrast, said its flight operations remained unaffected and that it had rerouted email traffic to maintain communication with customers.

The disruption also reached technology companies that rely on Microsoft's infrastructure. OpenAI and Anthropic reported problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, which enable their services to access workplace information, according to the reports. Businesses and government institutions in several countries reported difficulties carrying out everyday operations while email and workplace applications were unavailable.

What readers should do, and what happens next

If email sent during the outage has not arrived, Microsoft's own account suggests patience before escalation: restoration was phased, delayed traffic is still being cleared, and the 48-hour timeout window was extended specifically so delayed messages keep retrying instead of bouncing. Administrators can follow the incident on the Microsoft service health status page.

The next substantive step is Microsoft's promised post-incident report. The company said the report will follow once its review is complete. Until it appears, the confirmed account is narrow: a network capacity upgrade introduced the fault, a later network change brought it to the surface, and a staged restoration over more than 36 hours brought Microsoft 365 back.
